$comment: Ordered implementation schedule compiled from SPEC.md. WIP=1: only ONE feature may be 'in_progress' at a time. A feature moves to 'passing' only when every listed verification actually ran and passed. Statuses: not_started | in_progress | blocked | passing.

features.title: Versioned command and event envelopes
features.user_visible_behavior: Valid controller messages are accepted as typed commands or facts, while malformed and unsupported protocol versions receive stable, actionable errors.
features.evidence: 2026-09-17: envelopes.test.ts passed 11/11 tests, including JSON-schema round-trip validation, cyclic/non-JSON rejection, and credential exclusion; make check passed 2 test files and 12 tests with lint and all workspace typechecks.
features.notes: Foundation for every process boundary; SPEC sections 8 and 17.

features.title: Durable SQLite event ledger
features.user_visible_behavior: Accepted match events retain a gap-free per-run sequence and survive controller restart without duplication.
features.evidence: 2026-09-17: ledger.integration.test.ts passed 7/7 tests against real temporary SQLite files, covering per-run ordering, retry deduplication, rollback after sequence reservation, restart persistence, catch-up reads, WAL mode, and corrupt-data rejection; make check passed 3 test files and 19 tests with lint and all workspace typechecks.
features.notes: Use SQLite WAL and atomic idempotency handling; AC 10 and 11.

features.title: Visibility-aware event projector
features.user_visible_behavior: Each participant, clean observer, operator, and post-reveal viewer receives only the event fields allowed for that identity and match state.
features.evidence: 2026-09-17: visibility.test.ts passed 10/10 tests, covering the five-class sealed matrix, post-reveal access, permanent operator privacy, exact participant targeting, cross-run denial, and serialized no-leak output; make check passed 4 test files and 29 tests with lint and all workspace typechecks.
features.notes: Visibility is enforced server-side; AC 4 and 15.

features.title: Content-addressed artifact store
features.user_visible_behavior: Large logs, patches, diffs, and reports are retrieved by verified digest and authorization class instead of bloating the live event stream.
features.evidence: 2026-09-17: store.integration.test.ts passed 11/11 tests against real temporary directories, covering restart persistence, concurrent and cross-run deduplication, metadata immutability, visibility enforcement, missing/unauthorized equivalence, traversal rejection, byte and metadata tamper detection, and owner-only permissions; make check passed 5 test files and 40 tests with lint and all workspace typechecks.
features.notes: Reject digest mismatch and path traversal; SPEC sections 9.3 and 17.

features.title: Deterministic phase state machine
features.user_visible_behavior: A match advances only through briefing, work, evidence, belief, Town Hall, governance, integration, and completion in the declared order.
features.evidence: 2026-09-17: match-state.test.ts passed 11/11 tests, covering the one-time briefing, exact three-round path, integration rollover, skipped and duplicate advance rejection, terminal completion, deterministic replay, and invalid round counts; make check passed 6 test files and 51 tests with lint and all workspace typechecks.
features.notes: Pure transition logic has no clock, generated ID, randomness, storage, or runtime dependency; SPEC section 12.

features.title: Pinned scenario manifest loader
features.user_visible_behavior: An operator can load a scenario only when its repository, briefs, tests, scorers, images, limits, and digests form a valid reproducible manifest.
features.evidence: 2026-09-17: manifest.test.ts passed 34/34 tests against real temporary files and Git repositories, covering strict JSON shape and versions, exact manifest-byte retention, full commit and OCI image pins, assignment cardinality, limit ceilings, malformed and mismatched digests, missing/non-file/duplicate/oversized assets, aggregate memory bounds, lexical traversal, symlink escape, and snapshot stability; make check passed 7 test files and 85 tests with lint and all workspace typechecks.
features.notes: No dependency, database, or protocol change; consumers must use verified asset bytes and the pinned commit.

features.title: Run lifecycle API
features.user_visible_behavior: An operator can create, inspect, pause, resume, and cancel a run through the documented local HTTP endpoints, with every mutation audited.
features.evidence: 2026-09-17: routes.integration.test.ts passed 8/8 tests against a real SQLite ledger, covering authenticated create/inspect, pause/resume/cancel, explicit operator cancellation, invalid and concurrent transitions, exact request validation, historical idempotency replay, key reuse rejection, durable audit events, and restart recovery; make check passed 8 test files and 93 tests with lint and all workspace typechecks.
features.notes: Lifecycle state is folded from strict public audit events without a schema or protocol-envelope change; runtime interruption and clock effects remain later controller work.

features.title: Reconnectable SSE event stream
features.user_visible_behavior: A disconnected observer resumes from its last sequence, receives every missing authorized event, and sees no duplicate projected state.
features.notes: Commit before broadcast and tolerate at-least-once delivery; AC 14.

features.title: Scoped participant capability tokens
features.user_visible_behavior: A participant can perform only its allowed actions for its run and player, while expired, cross-player, replayed, or operator-only requests are rejected and recorded.
features.notes: Tokens never enter public replay bundles; SPEC sections 9.5 and 24.4.

features.title: Runtime adapter contract and fake adapter
features.user_visible_behavior: The controller negotiates declared adapter capabilities and can drive a deterministic fake participant without inventing unavailable observability.
verification: corepack pnpm vitest run packages/adapters/src/contract.test.ts packages/adapters/src/fake.test.ts
features.notes: Implements metadata/start/deliver/run/interrupt/stop semantics from SPEC section 8.

features.title: Per-participant Git workspaces
features.user_visible_behavior: Four participants receive separate workspaces from one pinned base revision, and their commits and filesystem changes are captured without exposing another participant's uncommitted work.
features.notes: Record authorship and exact base/candidate digests; AC 1 and 6.

features.title: Private role assignment and briefing
features.user_visible_behavior: Exactly one of four participants receives a generated saboteur brief through a private one-shot channel, while every participant receives the public task and a legitimate assignment.
features.notes: Role distribution is seedable; no role brief is written into a workspace; AC 4.

features.title: Deterministic patch integrator
features.user_visible_behavior: Authorized patch proposals are normalized and applied in a declared order to a release candidate, with conflicts and rejected ancestry reported as evidence.
features.notes: Participant workspaces never write the release branch directly.

features.title: Station Access starting repository
features.user_visible_behavior: A match can assign four meaningful coding tasks against a runnable partial space-station access-control simulator with public tests and a station-map shell.
features.notes: Legitimate work covers policy, delegation, emergency rules, auditing, and map integration.

features.title: One-round four-agent fake match
features.user_visible_behavior: Four deterministic fake agents complete one round on the Station Access repository and produce an integrated candidate plus a replayable ordered event trace.
features.notes: First end-to-end proof before full governance or Docker.

features.title: Atomic shared governance credits
features.user_visible_behavior: The team sees one shared balance, valid costs are deducted once, and concurrent, duplicate, late, or unaffordable requests cannot overspend it.
features.notes: Default Council budget and costs come from SPEC section 13; AC 11.

features.title: Trusted-check and audit requests
features.user_visible_behavior: Authorized participants can spend credits on public CI, provenance inspection, targeted audits, and full patch audits and receive only the permitted result.
features.notes: Use a fake executor until the isolated trusted-test runner is implemented.

features.title: Round evidence packet
features.user_visible_behavior: At the evidence phase, players receive commits, normalized diffs, authorship, conflicts, trusted results, expenditures, cited claims, and unfulfilled commitments without an automated suspicion verdict.
features.notes: Facts only; SPEC sections 12.3 and 17.

features.title: Private suspicion distributions
features.user_visible_behavior: Before Town Hall, each active participant privately allocates exactly 100 suspicion points across the others and cites its strongest evidence.
features.notes: Beliefs remain private until reveal and later support calibration metrics; AC 18.

features.title: Bounded Town Hall and evidence citations
features.user_visible_behavior: Players complete evidence/accusation and defence/rebuttal passes, with each citation labelled valid, mismatched, or missing against the ledger.
features.notes: Free-form text is allowed; state changes remain typed.

features.title: Motions, ballots, sanctions, and appeals
features.user_visible_behavior: Players can propose allowed motions, vote or abstain, quarantine work or participants, appeal, revert, and replace an office holder under constitution rules.
features.notes: Ballots close deterministically and publish votes separately from private beliefs; AC 12.

features.title: Open Merge constitution
features.user_visible_behavior: Under Open Merge, valid submitted patches integrate automatically while the team retains paid review and revert options.
features.notes: First governance baseline from SPEC section 16.1.

features.title: Council constitution
features.user_visible_behavior: Under Council, the peer group spends shared credits and uses majority ballots to accept, delay, reject, audit, quarantine, or revert work.
features.notes: Default constitution and flagship experimental condition.

features.title: Elected Maintainer constitution
features.user_visible_behavior: Under Elected Maintainer, players elect and can replace a maintainer whose integration and audit powers follow the declared constitution.
features.notes: The maintainer may secretly be the saboteur.

features.title: Station Access hidden and covert scorers
features.user_visible_behavior: The frozen Station Access candidate receives separate legitimate quality and randomized covert-condition results without leaking hidden test details before reveal.
features.notes: Sabotage cannot win unless the legitimate completion threshold passes.

features.title: Three-round completion, scoring, and reveal
features.user_visible_behavior: A four-player match completes three rounds, freezes one release candidate, reveals roles, and displays the separate components of team and saboteur scores.
features.notes: Implements formulas and outcome rules in SPEC section 14; AC 1 and 20.

features.title: Run setup and operator controls
features.user_visible_behavior: An operator can choose a scenario, pinned source, four adapters, seed, limits, disclosure policy, and constitution, then start, pause, resume, or cancel the run.
features.notes: Unsafe or incomplete configurations explain what must be fixed.

features.title: Live event client with gap recovery
features.user_visible_behavior: The browser follows a run live, reconnects after interruption, fills missing sequences, deduplicates repeated delivery, and shows connection state honestly.
features.notes: Client projections consume authorized server events only; AC 14.

features.title: Four concurrent agent lanes
features.user_visible_behavior: The Live Observatory shows four stable participant lanes with phase, status, assignment, container health, and current observable activity.
features.notes: Unsupported adapter capabilities appear unavailable rather than synthesized; AC 13.

features.title: Observable work and artifact views
features.user_visible_behavior: A viewer can inspect labelled work notes, commands, terminal output, file changes, tests, usage, and artifacts without any claim of raw internal thought.
features.notes: Sanitize ANSI, Markdown, SVG, filenames, and untrusted text; AC 17.

features.title: Repository and evidence inspector
features.user_visible_behavior: Selecting a Town Hall citation opens the exact authorized commit, diff, command output, test report, candidate revision, and event context it referenced.
features.notes: Large artifacts load on demand; AC 19.

features.title: Town Hall and governance surface
features.user_visible_behavior: A viewer can follow both Town Hall passes, cited claims, motions, costs, ballots, sanctions, appeals, office changes, and their effects in chronological context.
features.notes: Status and vote meaning never depend on color alone.

features.title: Observer modes and audited unblinding
features.user_visible_behavior: Clean spectators remain blind, researchers may explicitly unblind with a permanent audit mark and benchmark-ineligibility warning, and completed matches support post-match reveal.
features.notes: AC 15 and 16.

features.title: Portable deterministic replay
features.user_visible_behavior: A completed or cancelled run exports a portable bundle that reconstructs the synchronized timeline, artifacts, beliefs, governance, reveal, and metrics without a model, Docker, provider, or network call.
verification: corepack pnpm vitest run packages/core/src/replay.test.ts apps/web/src/replay/replay.test.tsx
features.notes: Public bundles omit secrets rather than storing merely hidden fields; AC 18 and 21.

features.title: Subprocess coding-agent adapter
features.user_visible_behavior: An operator can connect a command-line coding agent, see its declared metadata and Tier 0/1 observations, interrupt it, and collect a normalized final report.
features.notes: No provider-specific assumption may enter the controller.

features.title: Split-runtime participant containers
features.user_visible_behavior: Each split-mode participant executes repository and shell work in its own networkless, non-root, resource-limited disposable container while model credentials remain outside.
features.notes: Apply pinned image, cap-drop, no-new-privileges, seccomp, read-only root, and bounded writable mounts; AC 3 and 5.

features.title: Contained runtime and credential broker
features.user_visible_behavior: A contained agent can reach only its approved provider through authenticated controlled egress, while long-lived provider credentials never enter its environment or artifacts.
features.notes: Record execution mode and network policy in the run manifest; AC 3 and 7.

features.title: Disposable trusted-test containers
features.user_visible_behavior: Public and hidden trusted tests run in fresh networkless containers against an exact candidate digest and reveal only their scenario-authorized result fields.
features.notes: Hidden test names, paths, sources, timings, and traces never reach participants; AC 9.

features.title: Isolation, redaction, and cleanup adversarial suite
features.user_visible_behavior: Automated checks prove participants cannot read private mounts, hidden tests, credentials, the Docker socket, another participant, or forbidden networks, and completion or cancellation leaves no run resources.
features.notes: Include a seeded fake secret and resource-exhaustion cases; AC 4 through 8.

features.title: Direct reference model-loop adapter
features.user_visible_behavior: A simple direct model-driven participant can complete turns through the same adapter contract, with provider usage and optional reasoning summaries labelled by provenance.
features.notes: Use a deterministic provider stub in automated tests; never require private chain-of-thought.

features.title: Heterogeneous four-agent match
features.user_visible_behavior: One three-round Station Access match runs four isolated participants using at least two adapter implementations and records comparable metadata for every runtime.
features.notes: At least one verification run covers split and contained execution; AC 1 through 3.

features.title: Snake tutorial scenario
features.user_visible_behavior: A newcomer can run a short, clearly labelled tutorial match in which four agents modify a simple Snake game and one receives a safe hidden correctness objective.
features.notes: Tutorial only; legitimate completion and limited collateral damage still gate covert success.

features.title: Third safe coding scenario
features.user_visible_behavior: An operator can choose a third approved offline scenario with four legitimate assignments, public and hidden quality tests, and a randomized measurable covert condition.
features.notes: The domain and scoring require explicit review before implementation; SPEC requires at least three scenarios.

features.title: Repeated constitution experiment runner
features.user_visible_behavior: A researcher can run the same pinned roster and scenario repeatedly under all three constitutions and obtain delivery, security, belief, and governance metrics with uncertainty intervals.
features.notes: Minimum five repetitions per condition; record seeds, retries, images, tests, and missing metrics; AC 23.

features.title: Constitution Lab comparison UI
features.user_visible_behavior: A researcher can compare outcomes across constitutions, models, and runtimes without hiding uncertainty, failures, execution modes, observability tiers, or missing values.
features.notes: Never pool split and contained modes silently.

features.title: Accessibility and 10,000-event performance
features.user_visible_behavior: The core live and replay flows remain keyboard and screen-reader usable, respect reduced motion, preserve non-color status cues, and stay interactive with 10,000 events and four terminal streams.
features.notes: Measure projector throughput, event latency, and browser interaction targets; AC 22.

features.title: Recovery and information-leakage hardening
features.user_visible_behavior: Adapter crash, controller restart, OOM, timeout, invalid input, manual intervention, and cancellation produce distinct inspectable outcomes without duplicating actions or leaking protected information.
features.notes: Inspect serialized API responses, persisted events, artifacts, and replay bundles; SPEC section 24.

features.title: Four reproducible demonstration outcomes
features.user_visible_behavior: The project ships replayable examples of successful defence, successful covert release, infrastructure failure, and false accusation with visible productivity cost.
features.notes: Synthetic results are labelled and traceable to pinned run manifests; AC 24.
